t: This is Kensington Gore, a U-shaped thoroughfare on the south side of Hyde Park. Its streets connect the Royal Albert Hall with the Royal College of Art, the Royal Geographical Society, and, in Kensington Gardens, the Albert Memorial. The name comes from the Gore estate, which stood here until Victorian planners developed it in the mid 19th century. A gore is a narrow, triangular piece of land. Margaret Clive was born here in 1735. She went out to India to meet an admirer, and married a military hero. When they returned to England, the aristocracy did not welcome their new money.
